message.reasoning_content:
Let me plan: probe correctness across legal domain shapes, group sizes, non-monotone g_idx, arbitrary high nibbles, negative int32 words. Record a claim, run probe comparing run() vs reference().

Key risk: gemm group indexing — after sorting g_idx, group of kk in sorted order equals g_idx[order[kk]] which the kernel doesn't compute; it uses kk//GROUP_SIZE. Since sorting by g_idx gives contiguous groups aligned to group_size boundaries (histogram fixed: group g has exactly min(group_size,...) occurrences, so sorted g_idx is [0]*gs,[1]*gs,...), kk//GROUP_SIZE matches. Good.

Another risk: when scale is subnormal-ish FP16? scales in (0,1/32] fp16 fine.

Plan one comprehensive probe: sweep many shapes/seeds, compare against reference, compute max error vs tolerance. Also test negative qweight words (reference uses .long() handles; kernel uses uint32 cast — sign bits fine since only nibbles used).

Record claim then run probe.
